Geoffrey Wall, of Barrie, Ontario, is alleged to have operated as an airline captain between 2009 and 2025 without a license to fly large commercial passenger planes, according to Peel regional police.

About 20,000 people have signed a petition on Change.org entitled Protect Japanese Manga, protesting against the official White House X account posting videos featuring unauthorised use of imagery from the popular Dragon Ball, Yu-Gi-Oh! and Naruto series.

Footage published by China’s Xinhua state news agency showed an Air China plane carrying Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, touching down at Pyongyang’s Sunan international airport.

The pontiff arrived in Spain at the weekend for a week-long visit focused on immigration and politics.

rfi.description: Europe’s biggest companies are paying more than two-thirds of their profits to shareholders on average, diverting money that could otherwise support investment, climate action and workers’ wages, according to Oxfam.

rfi.title: France moves closer to ocean goals with three new marine protection zones
rfi.description: The French government has announced three new marine protected areas, bringing it a step closer to goals established at the 2025 United Nations Ocean Summit. After unsuccessful attempts in Switzerland, Platini is now turning to the French justice system to make his case.

lemonde.description: « On verra bien ce qu’il adviendra de l’accord. On était vraiment tout près d’un accord – mais ils n’arrêtent pas de nous mener en bateau », a lancé le président américain, interrogé au sujet de l’Iran.

lemonde.title: La France sans nouveau budget jusqu’à la présidentielle en 2027 : le scénario qui divise
lemonde.description: Les députés socialistes viennent de boucler une proposition de loi pour permettre à la France de tenir des mois si aucun budget ne peut être adopté. Le gouvernement, lui, ne veut pas entendre parler d’une nouvelle loi spéciale.

lemonde.title: Déserts médicaux : pourquoi l’accès aux médecins spécialistes reste sous tension

Les dépassements d’honoraires, en outre, créent une autre forme de « désert médical » de soins accessibles, avec des patients qui renoncent à se soigner pour des raisons de coût.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky participera au sommet du G7 mardi, annonce Emmanuel Macron

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : la FIFA accrédite le journaliste Christophe Gleizes, emprisonné en Algérie, pour médiatiser sa détention

lemonde.title: Camille F., docteure en épidémiologie qui a rejoint l’organisation Etat islamique en 2013, condamnée à douze ans de prison
lemonde.description: Le président de la cour d’assises spéciale de Paris a estimé dans son verdict que cette ancienne ingénieure, qui comparaissait détenue, et son mari Sylvain M., mort en 2015, avaient « choisi sciemment d’amener leurs enfants dans une zone de guerre ».

lemonde.title: Jean Ziegler, figure de la gauche suisse et critique du capitalisme, est mort à 92 ans
lemonde.description: Sociologue, écrivain, professeur à l’université de Genève et diplomate onusien, il s’est illustré par sa dénonciation du capitalisme « cannibale », des inégalités et du rôle parfois controversé de la place financière suisse.

lemonde.title: Vencorex : l’échec du projet de reprise de la plateforme chimique, malgré un soutien quasi unanime, relance le débat sur le fonctionnement des tribunaux de commerce
lemonde.description: Les porteurs du projet de relance du site de Pont-de-Claix (Isère) ont jeté l’éponge. Le juge n’est pas revenu sur sa décision de l’attribuer à un ferrailleur qui va vendre les installations à la découpe.

Plusieurs utilisateurs y voient une "humiliation raciste" à leur entrée sur le territoire américain. Ces images, véridiques, montrent en réalité un contrôle de routine pour les vols privés. La fédération de football sénégalaise a confirmé que cette procédure, opérée "sans incident", avait été organisée pour permettre aux joueurs d'éviter les files d'attente dans l'aérogare.

france24fr.title: Retour d’Omar Artan en héros à Mogadiscio : "Je serai là à la prochaine Coupe du monde" en 2030
france24fr.description: Omar Artane, l’arbitre somalien refoulé des États-Unis, est rentré chez lui. Il est arrivé en Somalie ce mercredi. Il a été accueilli en héros, en présence de plusieurs membres du gouvernement. Il a promis à ses soutiens qu’il participerait à la Coupe du monde 2030.

france24fr.title: Patrick Bruel mis en examen pour viol, tentative de viol, agression sexuelle et harcèlement sexuel
J-2 avant l'entrée en Bourse de SpaceX
france24fr.description: À l'occasion de son entrée en Bourse prévue le 12 juin, SpaceX espère lever 75 milliards de dollars et atteindre une valorisation de près de 1 800 milliards de dollars, ce qui en ferait l'introduction boursière la plus importante de l'histoire. L'opération est très attendue par les investisseurs, mais également redoutée par certains en raison du manque de rentabilité de la compagnie d'Elon Musk.

france24fr.title: Bilan carbone: le Mondial 2026 sera le plus émetteur de gaz à effet de serre de l'Histoire
france24fr.description: Selon le dossier de candidature, le Mondial 2026 devait être le moins polluant de l'Histoire. Il pourrait être, à l'inverse, le plus émetteur de gaz à effet de serre. La faute aux nombreux kilomètres avalés en avion entre des stades répartis sur tout le continent nord-américain. La faute aussi au nombre record d'équipes participantes (porté de 32 à 48). +92% d'émissions pour cette édition par rapport à la moyenne des décennies précédentes selon l'association SGR.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la vidéo de la fouille des joueurs sénégalais a "indigné toute la communauté africaine"
france24fr.description: Une vidéo montrant des joueurs de l'équipe nationale de football sénégalaise se faire fouiller sur le tarmac d’un aéroport américain a massivement été partagée sur les réseaux sociaux. Beaucoup d'internautes se sont insurgés contre un traitement "humiliant". L'équipe du Sénégal a démenti mais la polémique perdure, notamment avec le relais d’intox.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : les souvenirs les plus marquants des journalistes de France 24
france24fr.description: La Coupe du monde de football 2026 est sur le point de débuter... C'est donc l'occasion parfaite pour se remémorer ses souvenirs les plus marquants en Mondial !

france24fr.title: Mort de Lyhanna : un échec national ?
france24fr.description: Face à l'immense émotion suscitée par la mort de la jeune Lyhanna, 11 ans, dont les obsèques se tiendront vendredi dans l'intimité familiale, le gouvernement français et la justice font l'objet de vives critiques en raison des défaillances présumées de plusieurs institutions, notamment judiciaires. En visite mercredi dans une unité spécialisée de l'hôpital pédiatrique Hôpital Robert-Debré à Paris, E. Macron a estimé qu'il fallait en faire davantage pour "protéger" les enfants des violences.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : NBA, NFL, mode… Le rêve américain des stars du football
france24fr.description: De Buff Donelli à Kylian Mbappé, les footballeurs et les États-Unis entretiennent une histoire d'amour depuis près d’un siècle. Alors que les stars du ballon rond s'affichent dans les salles de la NBA et deviennent ambassadeurs du football américain, le mariage entre ces deux mondes n'a jamais semblé aussi pertinent.

france24fr.title: France : 30 ans de prison pour tentative de meurtre d'un dissident azerbaïdjanais
france24fr.description: Une cour d'assises spéciale à Rennes a condamné mercredi à trente ans de réclusion criminelle Emin Gasimov, considéré comme le "chef" du commando ayant tenté d'assassiner en 2021 à Nantes le blogueur azerbaïdjanais dissident Mahammad Mirzali.

france24fr.title: Darmanin renonce au "plaider-coupable" criminel après le rejet du texte en commission
france24fr.description: Alors que son projet de loi a été rejeté mercredi en commission, le ministre de la Justice Gérald Darmanin, qui fait face aux critiques liées à l'affaire Lyhanna, a annoncé retirer la mesure phare de son texte, le "plaider-coupable" pour les infractions les plus graves.

france24fr.title: Un sac à main en cuir de tyrannosaure mis aux enchères à Paris
france24fr.description: Un sac à main, façonné dans une matière biosynthétique, a été conçu à partir de traces de collagène retrouvées dans un fémur de T-Rex aux États-Unis. Cette pièce unique est estimée entre 300 000 et 500 000 euros et sera mise aux enchères à l’hôtel des ventes Drouot à Paris ce jeudi.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'équipe du Sénégal visée par des intox venant de supporters marocains
france24fr.description: La vidéo d'un contrôle de sécurité dans un aéroport de l'équipe du Sénégal aux États-Unis est la cible d'intox relayées par des supporters marocains. Ils affirment à tort que les joueurs sénégalais ont été humiliés lors d'une fouille en partageant pour preuve une photo créée par IA et un faux article.

france24fr.title: Iran : Trump et l'accord jamais conclu ?
france24fr.description: Donald trump affirme que Téhéran a été trop lent dans les négociations et que le pays va en payer le prix, alors que l'Iran a revendiqué des attaques contre des bases américaines notamment au Bahrein. Les explications avec Jonathan Piron, historien, conseiller au centre de recherche Etopia de Bruxelles, spécialiste des relations internationales et du Moyen-Orient

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026: les joueurs sénégalais contrôlés sur le tarmac d'un aéroport, la fédération réagit
france24fr.description: Une vidéo montrant les joueurs du #Sénégal engagés dans la #CoupeduMonde passant un contrôle de sécurité sur le tarmac d'un aéroport aux #ÉtatsUnis avait suscité des accusations de #racisme. Mais selon la fédération, il s'agissait bien de contrôles réglementaires visant à accélérer le déplacement de la sélection.

france24fr.title: Irlande du Nord : les violences xénophobes, symptômes d'une "malheureuse normalisation de ces idées"
france24fr.description: À Belfast, de violentes émeutes anti-immigration ont éclaté mardi soir après l'inculpation d'un réfugié soudanais pour une attaque au couteau, sur fond d'appels à manifester relayés par des figures de l'extrême droite. Écoles fermées, transports à l'arrêt... la ville redoute une escalade. Décryptage avec Fabrice Mourlon, professeur à l’université Sorbonne-Nouvelle et spécialiste de l'Irlande du Nord.

france24fr.title: Au fond de l'océan Indien, un stupéfiant cimetière de baleines
france24fr.description: Une étude publiée mercredi dans la revue scientifique Nature relate la découverte du plus grand cimetière de baleines connu au monde avec près de 500 squelettes répartis sur un corridor long de 1 200 kilomètres, à l'Ouest de l'Australie. Les scientifiques pensent que les baleines sont mortes en si grand nombre dans cette zone parce qu'il s'agit d'une aire d'alimentation importante.

france24fr.title: La foule se presse alors que le pape va bénir la Sagrada Familia
france24fr.description: "C’est comme si c’était Dieu, l’Esprit saint." À Barcelone, la foule se presse pour assister à la bénédiction de la Sagrada Familia par le pape Leon XIV. Notre correspondante Maude Petit-Jové s’est rendue sur place.

nzz.description: Anders als die Gewerkschaften vor der Abstimmung flöteten, ist die 13. AHV-Rente nicht gratis zu haben. Die Bürgerlichen sollten sich bei der Finanzierung nun nicht unter Druck setzen lassen.

nzz.description: Nördlich von München sind am Mittwoch zwei Busse kollidiert. Mehrere Kinder wurden mittelschwer bis schwer verletzt.

nzz.title: Die Angst vor der Inflation ist eine zweite Chance für Christine Lagarde

nzz.description: Das Ringen um die AHV nähert sich dem Ende. Mitte und SP haben sich in der Einigungskonferenz durchgesetzt. Die finanziellen Folgen für die Privathaushalte wären sehr unterschiedlich.

nzz.title: Trump laviert im Nahen Osten zwischen Vergeltung und Friedensgesprächen
nzz.description: Amerikanische Streitkräfte beschiessen militärische Einrichtungen Irans in der Nähe der Strasse von Hormuz. Iran antwortet mit Raketen auf Bahrain, Kuwait und Jordanien. Ist das nun das Ende der seit Wochen andauernden Verhandlungen um ein Kriegsende?

nzz.title: Messerangriff in Belfast heizt rassistische Spannungen in Grossbritannien weiter an
nzz.description: Ein sudanesischer Asylbewerber hat in Belfast einen Mann niedergestochen. Die Tat befeuert die ohnehin aufgeheizte Debatte über die britische Migrationspolitik.

nzz.description: 2023 waren Plagiatsvorwürfe gegen die frisch gewählte Nationalrätin erhoben worden. Jetzt ist klar: Fehr Düsel kommt mit einem blauen Auge davon. Steigt sie nun ins Rennen um den Ständerat?

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die markante Vergrösserung der WM ist ein Erfolg: Mehr Fussball macht mehr Menschen glücklich
nzz.description: Ab Donnerstag spielen an der Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft erstmals 48 Nationen um den Titel. Die Erweiterung schadet dem sportlichen Niveau in der Vorrunde. Aber die gesellschaftlichen und ökonomischen Vorteile machen das mehr als wett.

spiegel.title: ICE: Donald Trump stattet US-Einwanderungsbehörden mit zusätzlichen 70 Milliarden Dollar aus
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat den »Secure America Act« unterzeichnet und stellt 70 Milliarden Dollar für Einwanderungsbehörden wie ICE bereit. Damit ist die brutale Abschiebepolitik bis zum Ende seiner Amtszeit finanziert.

spiegel.description: Das Portal »Frag den Staat« hat Auffälligkeiten in Texten von Thüringens Ministerpräsident Mario Voigt entdeckt. Weil die Staatskanzlei Fragen auswich, löschte die »FAZ« nun einen Gastbeitrag.

spiegel.title: Noma in Kopenhagen: Weltberühmtes Restaurant will im August wieder öffnen
spiegel.description: Für viele galt das Noma in Kopenhagen als das beste Restaurant der Welt. Im März schloss es, vorher hatte es Gewaltvorwürfe gegen Küchenchef Rédzepi gegeben. Im August öffnet es nun wieder – mit einem neuen Küchenchef.

spiegel.description: In Southampton fordern Demonstranten Abschiebungen, in Belfast brennen Häuser und Autos: Aus Kritik an einer angeblich zu woken Polizei wird Hass gegen Migranten.

spiegel.description: Jean Ziegler war der bekannteste und umstrittenste Intellektuelle der Schweiz – und wurde berühmt durch seinen Kampf gegen das Bankgeheimnis und den globalen Hunger. Nun ist er im Alter von 92 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.description: Die Tierschützer Anna Schubert und Hendrik Haßel wurden beim heimlichen Filmen erwischt, verurteilt – und gingen in Berufung. Nun hat ein Gericht erneut entschieden.

spiegel.description: Das deutsch-französische Projekt FCAS ist gescheitert. Frankreich will die bereitgestellten Mittel nun für die Entwicklung eines eigenen Kampfjets nutzen.

spiegel.title: FCAS: Airbus hofft nach Projekt-Aus auf neuen Kampfjetauftrag
spiegel.description: Nach dem Aus für den gemeinsamen Kampfjet mit Frankreich prescht die deutsche Industrie vor. Doch Kanzler Merz hält sich beim Rundgang auf der Luftfahrtmesse ILA alle Optionen offen.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM in den USA: Deutsche Spitzenpolitiker meiden die Trump-WM
spiegel.description: Deutsche Spitzenpolitiker besuchen Spiele des Nationalteams, einst war das üblich bei Fußball-Weltmeisterschaften im Ausland. Nicht so diesmal: Vorerst reist nur die zuständige Staatsministerin an.

spiegel.title: Jean Ziegler: Schweizer Soziologe und Autor ist tot
spiegel.description: Er galt zeitlebens als Fürsprecher der Entmachteten und als streitbarer Gegner der Profitgier – und polarisierte damit. Nun ist der Soziologe, Autor und frühere Politiker Jean Ziegler gestorben.

spiegel.description: Auch sein Name taucht in den Epstein-Akten auf: Deswegen sagt Bill Gates vor einem Untersuchungsausschuss des US-Repräsentantenhauses aus. Vorgeworfen wird ihm nichts.

spiegel.description: Zum 1. Mai führte die Bundesregierung einen Tankrabatt ein. Damit sollten die Folgen des Irankriegs abgemildert werden. Jetzt ist klar: Die Steuersenkung endet.

wired.description: According to new research, Trionda would show less unpredictable movements in actions such as corner kicks or free kicks. However, in powerful and long-distance clearances it would lose range.

new-sci.description: Europe’s largest land animal, the bison, is thought to be relatively unthreatened by predators, but footage from Białowieża Primaeval Forest in Poland shows it does face attacks from wolves

new-sci.title: Millions of fossil whale bones found in deep-ocean ‘necropolis’
new-sci.description: Researchers diving 7 kilometres deep in a crewed submersible have discovered a vast collection of whale bones, including fossils up to 5 million years old and species new to science

new-sci.title: Hundreds of new moons are revealing our solar system's violent history
new-sci.description: The outer solar system once seemed like a quiet backwater. But a glut of tiny, strange moons with unruly orbits are coming into view, revealing hints of a surprising past – and the origin of Saturn's rings

new-sci.title: A nuclear war between India and Pakistan could destroy the ozone layer
new-sci.description: Climate models suggest a small nuclear war in the tropics would do even more damage to the ozone layer than a larger nuclear war in more northerly latitudes, increasing exposure to dangerous ultraviolet radiation all over the world

new-sci.title: A Waymo nearly hit me, but I'm still optimistic about driverless cars
new-sci.description: A near miss with a Waymo while cycling through London hasn't changed my optimistic stance on driverless cars, but we can't ever let our guard down, says Matthew Sparkes

new-sci.title: Robots are about to overtake armed soldiers as the deciders of war
new-sci.description: Uncrewed ground vehicles have already been tested for defending the front line by the Ukrainian military. Despite their limitations, these remotely controlled robots could be the deciding factor in many conflicts

new-sci.title: Iron Age Britons may have removed the brains of the dead
new-sci.description: Scrape marks inside a skull and sharpened limb bones in a set of remains found in Scotland may be evidence of unusual Iron Age funerary rituals

new-sci.title: Frozen squirrel scat preserves ancient DNA from hundreds of species
new-sci.description: A complex ecosystem of woolly mammoths, bison, horses and big cats has been elucidated by studying the faeces of small rodents that probably ate the bigger animals

new-sci.title: The last-ditch plan to save coral reefs from utter destruction
new-sci.description: Bleaching has devastated reefs around the world, raising fears of an irreversible shift. Yet new interventions have revealed that corals can be remarkably resilient if we can give them enough help to recover

new-sci.title: Why we should all take quantum physics extremely personally
new-sci.description: Physics is considered a cold, hard science – but it will transform your life if you view it with a bit more subjectivity, says Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

new-sci.title: A cosmic case of mistaken identity that can only be solved right now
new-sci.description: Brown dwarfs are somewhere between the size of a planet and a star, so how could we have potentially mistaken two of them for distant galaxies? Columnist Chanda Prescod-Weinstein argues that solving this cosmic mix-up is particularly possible now, as galaxy research has never been stronger

new-sci.title: Dinosaur-killing asteroid impact site stayed hot for millions of years
new-sci.description: Drill cores at the impact site of the Chicxulub asteroid show evidence that, alongside widespread destruction, the collision created a vast underground ecosystem filled with hot water that sheltered microbial life

new-sci.title: Unpicking endometriosis reveals how it affects more than the pelvis
new-sci.description: Endometriosis is usually thought of as a gynaecological condition, but a huge study shows it has links with cholesterol levels, inflammation and an altered microbiome

new-sci.title: You don't need to worry about recursive-self-improving AI – yet
new-sci.description: Anthropic has warned that recursive-self-improving AI could be on the horizon, but the truth is the company is more immediately concerned with marketing itself for a blockbuster initial public offering on the stock market, says Matthew Sparkes

new-sci.title: What really happened when ancient humans migrated out of Africa
new-sci.description: The out-of-Africa migration, in which ancient humans went on to inhabit every other continent except Antarctica, may not have been one moment in time, but a long and slow process. Columnist Michael Marshall examines how archaeologists are rethinking this critical part of our history

new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?
new-sci.description: Lapses in memory are a normal part of ageing but can also be signs of dementia. Here’s how to distinguish between typical brain ageing and cognitive decline

new-sci.title: Wildlife thrives in solar farm built on restored peatland
new-sci.description: A diverse range of bird species has been recorded at a solar park on rewetted peatland in Germany, suggesting that combining energy generation with habitat restoration could benefit biodiversity, the climate and the economy

phys-org.title: Cells have a secret power line: How the nucleus gets its own private energy supply from mitochondria
phys-org.description: For decades, biologists assumed a cell's energy simply diffused to wherever it was needed. It turns out the most important destination of all has a private delivery line.

phys-org.title: Biopolymer beads extend fungus bioinsecticide shelf life and release
phys-org.description: Researchers have used a biopolymer to encapsulate and extend the storage life and release rate of a bioinsecticidal fungus. The study is published in ACS Omega. The goal is to extend the shelf life of Beauveria bassiana, a fungus widely used as a bioinsecticide on various agricultural crops. Encapsulation is also a more sustainable alternative because it requires fewer applications and has less potential to affect nontarget species.

phys-org.title: Borneo's ferret badger is found nowhere else on Earth
phys-org.description: A collaborative study has provided the most comprehensive assessment to date of the endangered Bornean ferret badger (Melogale everetti). Weighing only around one kilogram (2.2 pounds), the Bornean ferret badger is a small, nocturnal carnivore that is rarely seen by people. The paper is published in the journal Ecology and Evolution.

phys-org.title: Drone surveys reveal why steep alpine channels erode so fast during debris flows
phys-org.description: A brown mass—a mixture of water, boulders and fine matter—plows through the landscape. The mountains wash more than a thousand lorryloads of material into the valley on a fairly regular basis, causing damage in excess of CHF 100 million per year in Switzerland alone. A better understanding of this natural hazard requires data from the debris flow channels, of which there is very little because of the complex surveying process.

phys-org.title: X-rays reveal how platinum oxidizes in real time inside hydrogen devices
phys-org.description: Electrolysers produce hydrogen. Fuel cells, in turn, generate electricity from hydrogen. Both technologies are considered key building blocks of the energy transition, offering well-established solutions for storing, transporting and producing renewable energy. However, there is a challenge: The platinum catalysts often used in these systems gradually lose performance under high operating loads. In a sense, they "wear out" too quickly, increasing the costs of hydrogen technologies.

phys-org.title: Missing the forest for the trees: Conservationists emphasize the need for intact forest in coffee landscapes
phys-org.description: As conservationists seek to maintain biodiversity levels in tropical coffee landscapes, data indicate the presence and quality of surrounding forest habitat may play a larger role than previously thought. New research from the Colombian Andes shows that conserving forest cover across coffee-growing landscapes is essential for sustaining diverse bird communities, even more than farm-level shade tree management alone.

phys-org.title: AI helps reveal large-scale quantum effects hidden in stacked atomic sheets
phys-org.description: Quantum materials are a class of exotic materials with special properties that are governed by quantum mechanics rather than classical physics. Those properties—like superconductivity, entanglement and unusual forms of magnetism—often originate in the tiny repeating patterns of atoms inside crystals, but through clever engineering, they can be observed and controlled at a more human scale. Quantum materials are helping to power the quickly growing field of quantum computing and could find their

phys-org.title: Farm fields become living labs as data tools reshape crop research
phys-org.description: For generations, agronomic knowledge has been produced on research stations like AU Flakkebjerg, where fields are designed to answer specific scientific questions. This is where agriculture became measurable, comparable and reproducible. But a quiet shift is underway. Today, experiments are escaping the confines of the research station, turning ordinary farm fields into laboratories and farmers into active contributors to agricultural research.

phys-org.title: Antiviral soil compound disrupts phage infection cycle before viruses can reproduce
phys-org.description: Bacteria also produce molecules that have an antiviral effect. Researchers from Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU) and Jülich Research Center (FZJ) have examined the antiviral molecule daunorubicin and decoded its mode of operation against viruses in collaboration with colleagues from Marburg and Zurich. They now describe this mechanism, which primarily targets a specific group of viruses—namely bacteriophages—in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Australia adds 33 spiny crayfish species to threatened list after megafires
phys-org.description: To the scientists and ecologists working to save them, Australia's Euastacus crayfish species are fascinating, living relics from a time long ago.

phys-org.title: Archaeologists uncover 4,000-year-old evidence of siege warfare in ancient Mesopotamia
phys-org.description: At Kurd Qaburstan, an ancient site in the Kurdistan region of Iraq, archaeologists have uncovered the first substantial group of cuneiform administrative tablets found in the Erbil region, along with evidence of large-scale destruction, mass graves and citywide fortifications. Together, the discoveries are providing one of the clearest archaeological records yet uncovered of siege warfare and urban life during the Middle Bronze Age.

phys-org.title: Open-source FLIM Playground could speed reproducible analysis of complex cell images
phys-org.description: Modern fluorescence microscopy can generate images of living cells as stunning to look at as they are informative to study. For techniques like fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), those images provide a window into cell metabolism, helping scientists study cancer treatment, autoimmune disease and more.

phys-org.title: Algorithm visualizes how cells 'talk' to one another across tissue and time
phys-org.description: People communicate with each other, sometimes face to face, sometimes with a text message or phone call. Cells also communicate with each other, sometimes by touching and sometimes by sending signals across space and time. But while texts and phone calls can be traced to figure out who is talking to whom, determining which cell is talking to which is exceedingly difficult—until now.

phys-org.title: Gorillas can learn to trust humans even after years of poaching pressure, research shows
phys-org.description: A new study led by Concordia researchers suggests that carefully habituating wild gorillas to nonthreatening humans can help the animals overcome long-term aversions to people in areas with a history of human-led disturbances such as poaching.

phys-org.title: How anti-CRISPR proteins promote the spread of hospital-acquired infections
phys-org.description: Researchers from Skoltech—a VEB.RF group institution—and their colleagues from the U.S. and China have explained how the antibiotic resistance gene established itself in the genome of the bacterium Klebsiella pneumoniae. The findings could help control this widespread microbe, which can cause pneumonia, meningitis and other, often hospital-acquired, infections in patients with weakened immunity. The findings were reported in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Report: ICE surges have triggered massive job losses—including among Americans
phys-org.description: Since January 2025, the Trump administration has ramped up immigration enforcement. A key rationale for the policy is that it will open up jobs for Americans by reducing competition from undocumented immigrants.

phys-org.title: AI model 'hears' Bryde's whale calls in seismic data from South China Sea
phys-org.description: Researchers have repurposed an AI model designed for visual identification tasks to detect Bryde's whale calls contained within seismic data collected in the South China Sea. The detection system precisely identified calls more than 96% of the time and even identified some call events that were missed when the data were examined by hand, according to the study published in Seismological Research Letters.

phys-org.title: Everyone wants to think they're open‑minded. Here's why most people aren't
phys-org.description: Most people think they are open-minded and would like others to perceive them as such. But for the things that matter most—religious beliefs, for example, or the meaning of life—few of us are genuinely willing to consider that we might be wrong, let alone do the hard work of revising beliefs. At a fundamental level, we humans are somewhat closed-minded.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

- by Aeon Video

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. Yet income convergence with advanced economies has been painfully slow—and in most cases absent.

proj-syn.title: Is the US Stock Market Too Big?
proj-syn.description: With China and India having grown so fast as to compensate for the underperformance of their fellow BRICS (Brazil, Russia, and South Africa), the center of gravity in the global economy continues to shift eastward. The question now is whether—and when—equity valuations will reflect this underlying reality.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so.
